title: The story: thirteen acts
by: Dev (local model), checked by the writing room

items.told: Elder Mo found the first shard of nanite dust in your blood tonight. He stands by the fire, waiting for your answer.
items.say:
The world beneath our feet is not rock and root. It is a machine we do not control.

Every child born here has these tiny tools running in their veins. We are living inside a cage built by something ancient.

Do I tell the villagers? They will panic, or they might try to tear us down before we even understand what this is.
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a:
Mo nods grimly. He walks out to敲响 the bell that calls the whole town together.
(Trust is fragile, but transparency is safer.)
items.after_b:
Mo lights a candle for you alone. The secret stays heavy in your chest.
(Panic can be avoided, but fear grows quietly.)

items.told: Elder Mo stands in the candlelight of his small room, waiting for your decision. He holds a vial of swirling black fluid he calls nanite seed.
items.say: The deep put something inside every child born here forty years ago. They sleep in our blood and grow in our stone. I can tell them the truth about it, or I can keep us all asleep.
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: Mo pours half the vial into the well; the villagers stare at the black water with wide eyes.
items.after_b: Mo locks the door and wipes his hands; the fear in Eliet goes deeper, but we sleep.

items.told: Elder Mo sat by the fire, his hands shaking from the chill in the valley air. He waited for a word to settle the fear of what lies beneath Eliet.
items.say: The deep is not empty. Nanites sleep in your blood since before we drew breath, and they grow hungry if left unspoken. The first expedition found them forty years ago, yet we treat this gift like poison every day. I ask you to decide: does the village know the truth of their own veins, or do we keep our peace by pretending?
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: Mo lit a lantern for everyone, and Elder Lin began teaching the children how to feel the hum in their bones. Fear turned to purpose.
items.after_b: Mo tucked the lantern under his arm and walked to the edge of town alone. The silence around Eliet grew heavy again.

items.told: The village waits for Elder Mo to speak of the deep things beneath Eliet. The wind howls through the hills, but the truth is colder than any storm.
items.say: The nanites in your blood did not grow by accident. They were planted here when the world was young. Some say we are machines made flesh; others say we are souls given steel. Do you wish to keep the fear? Or do you wish to know what drives our bones?
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: You tell the people that their bodies hold the secret of survival, and trust grows in the square.
items.after_b: You whisper the secret to Elder Mo alone, and the village sleeps easier though the fear remains.

items.told: The deep hummed below Eliet as if breathing a secret. Elder Mo waits by the fire, his eyes dim with the knowledge of nanites in every child.
items.say: Nanites sleep in our blood since the world was seeded long ago. They are not magic, just tools the Deep left us. I saw them bloom in my veins when I first touched the dungeon floor. Some say they save us from the dark things below. Others fear we are already changed by the metal within.
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: Mo nods slowly, knowing the people must understand their own bodies to survive. He will teach them how to feel the machines pulse in their veins.
items.after_b: Mo looks away into the cold fire, hoping the fear of the unknown keeps everyone sleeping soundly.

items.told: Captain Rhee waits for your answer in the creaking guardhouse. The rival squad stands ready at the gate.
items.say: A messenger from Ironroot Hold asks for your permission to enter Eliet. They bring steel and hunger. I have my eyes on them all, but they outnumber me by two. Do you wish me to open the gates? Or do I tell them we hold nothing for traitors?
items.choice_b: Send word. I've nothing to prove.
items.after_a: The gates creak open; the rival squad enters, and Captain Rhee watches their leader with a cold nod.
items.after_b: Rhee sends a rider away with a warning note; the rival force retreats into the hills without striking.

items.told: You stood before Elder Mo in the quiet garden. He confessed the cost of your victory at the Jade Pagoda, waiting for your judgment on his words.
items.say: The pagoda is silent now. I brought you back what saved us, yet the town fears my face. Do you think a man should bear this secret alone? Or do we share the burden?
items.choice_a: I forgive you. You brought back what saved us.
items.after_a: The tension leaves his shoulders; he thanks you and offers to teach the next generation.
items.after_b: He looks away, ashamed, as the village gossip begins to spread before the sun rises.

items.told: The elder stands before the broken entrance to the Jade Pagoda, his hand trembling on the stone. You have brought him the proof from the deep: the truth that saved Eliet is now in your hands.
items.say:
You hold the confession of the first descent. They say I must choose between our safety and our pride. The town watches my face like a hawk. Tell me what you would do if you stood where I stand.

If I speak the truth, the village knows the cost of power. If I keep it quiet, we live in fear but sleep without nightmares. What is better for Eliet?
items.choice_a: I forgive you. You brought back what saved us.
items.after_a: Elder Mo nods once, tears mixing with the dust on his face. 'Then we carry this burden together,' he says before disappearing into the dark to heal the town.
items.after_b: Mo's shoulders slump, and he turns away from the Pagoda entrance. 'Pride will kill us all in the end,' a voice whispers from the wind as you walk toward the village square.

items.told: Captain Rhee stands by the heavy iron doors of the Lodge. The nine survivors of the first descent wait below.
items.say:
The deep has claimed seven more souls this season. I have picked six new faces from our list to go down with me. They are eager, but perhaps too eager for a place that eats hope. Do you want them sent to their deaths? Or do you keep them safe in Eliet?

I will lead them myself. Pick your six companions for the trip.
items.choice_a: I'll lead them. Pick your six.
items.choice_b: Keep them home. The deep is mine to carry.
items.after_a: The expedition leaves with fresh blood and new hope. Captain Rhee nods, satisfied that his name remains known among the living.
items.after_b: You keep the newcomers safe in the village. Captain Rhee sighs, watching the door you closed behind the new recruits.

items.told: Smith Hale stands by the forge, the last ingot glowing blue against the dark. The village waits to see if we can finish the seal tonight.
items.say: The deep below has taken its toll, but the nanites in our blood still hold fast. If we do not pour this steel now, the dungeon will swallow Eliet whole again. You have done well enough to stand here, traveler. Now tell me: are you ready to walk into the dark one more time?
items.choice_a: Through the night, then. Let's make it.
items.choice_b: Finish it your way. I'll rest.
items.after_a: Hale nods and begins hammering the final seal while you guard the door, the cold air biting at your clothes.
items.after_b: He sighs heavily, leaving the forge to cool as he steps out into the valley wind.

items.told: Apothecary Lin stares at his mortar, waiting for your decision on the bitter draught. The coughing fits in Eliet have grown louder since the expedition returned.
items.say:
The deep sickness burns like fire in cold water, yet it is our own blood that feeds it. I made this medicine from the nanite dust collected from the deepest floors. It will clear your lungs if you can swallow the taste of iron. Do not waste my work on pride or fear.

Some say the village knows best, but truth often tastes bitter before it heals.
items.choice_a: Make the draught. I'll drink it with them.
items.after_a: Lin mixes the powder and hands you the vial; you swallow the metallic taste together as Eliet's coughing eases.
items.after_b: Lin pockets the ingredients, leaving the cure for others to find on their own while you walk away with silence.

items.told: Elder Mo stands by your door, holding a sealed jar of nanites. The village waits for his verdict on what they are.
items.say:
You carry the Deep's gift now. But do you let Eliet know? Or does the secret keep us safe from panic?

The first expedition died so this blood could live. If we tell the truth, fear spreads like fire in dry grass.

If we hide it, the people sleep easier, but they carry a poison they cannot name.

What is your choice?
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: Mo opens the jar for all to see. The townsfolk whisper, their faces pale as snow.
items.after_b: Mo seals the lid tight again. He nods to you, and the silence returns to the valley.

items.told: Elder Mo waits by the hearth, his eyes dark with what he saw in the deep. The town sleeps, unaware that nanites swim in our blood and stone.
items.say: We found the truth down there. It is heavy to carry, but hiding it will rot us from within. Do we tell the villagers what lives beneath their feet? Or do we let fear keep them safe? Speak now, before the night claims another soul.
items.choice_a: The village should know the truth.
items.after_a: Mo nods slowly, a grim resolve settling on his face. He steps out into the dark to warn the sleeping town. (Trust is fragile, but honesty is stronger.)
items.after_b: Mo looks away, closing his eyes tight against the weight of silence. He vows no one else will hear the secrets of the deep again. (Fear keeps us safe, for now.)
